title: Let me sign in instead of bookmarking a private admin link
body:
Owner request. Today a wall is managed through a private link that people must bookmark; if they lose it (new phone, cleared browser, another device) they lose their wall. Simulated users hit this too.

Use the engine's accounts capability (Clerk, see BRIEF.md: `clerkHead`, `currentUser`) so people can sign in and see all their walls from any device. Keep it optional and fast: creating a wall without an account should keep working, and existing private links must keep working. Offer to attach a wall to an account (e.g. right after creating it, or from the manage page).

title: Sell Kudospage Pro: pricing page with a real checkout
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. Use the engine's payments capability (BRIEF.md → Payments; `payScript`, `dwPay.open`, `payReady`, `paidSkus`). On /pricing show Free vs Pro with both offers from species.json: `pro_monthly` ($9 per month, cancel any time) and `pro_lifetime` ($49 once). Each gets a clear button that calls `dwPay.open(sku, {next: '/pricing?welcome=pro'})` on click; when `dwPay.ready` is false show 'Coming soon' plus the existing email list instead of a dead button. Add 'Already bought? Unlock it here' linking to `dwPay.restoreUrl`. Paddle reviews the live site before enabling checkout, so also: say on /pricing and /terms that payments are handled by Paddle (merchant of record, receipts, cancellations, refunds); add a plain refund policy (full refund within 14 days, reply to the receipt) on /terms or a /refunds page linked from the footer; mention Paddle on /privacy. Remove 'Not available yet' wording once the buttons exist. Keep everything that is free today free.

title: Pro unlocks: no badge and own colours on the widget
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. Deliver what Pro promises, using `paidSkus(c)` (server) / `dwPay.has(sku)` (browser), either sku counts. Walls created or managed by a Pro buyer show the widget and public wall without the 'Powered by Kudospage' badge, and let them pick their own accent colour and font (stored per wall; a migration may add columns). The wall must remember it is Pro even when the owner manages it from another browser later: store the Pro status on the wall when a paying visitor creates/manages it (and when they sign in, on their account). Non-paying walls keep working exactly as today. Tests with `x-test-paid: pro_lifetime`.

title: Offer Pro at the moment it is useful (honestly)
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. People only think about the badge once they see their widget on their own site. On the manage page next to the embed code, and on the public wall preview, add one calm, dismissible line: 'Want it without the Kudospage badge and in your colours? Pro is $9/month or $49 once.' linking to /pricing (or opening checkout directly). No pop-ups, no countdowns, no nagging after it's dismissed. Measure with dw.track.

title: Sell CalmCV Pro: pricing page with a real checkout
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. Use the engine's payments capability (BRIEF.md → Payments). On /pricing keep 'Building and downloading your resume as PDF is free' as the headline promise, and add CalmCV Pro: `pro_pass`, $9 once, no subscription, with exactly what it adds (matching cover letter builder, several saved resume versions, Word .docx export). Button calls `dwPay.open('pro_pass', {next: '/builder?welcome=pro'})` (or the builder's real path) on click; when `dwPay.ready` is false show 'Coming soon' plus the existing email list. Add 'Already bought? Unlock it here' → `dwPay.restoreUrl`. Paddle reviews the site before enabling checkout: state on /pricing and /terms that Paddle handles payment, receipts and refunds; add a plain refund policy (full refund within 14 days, reply to the receipt) on /terms or /refunds; mention Paddle on /privacy. Update the 'maybe later' wording, which is no longer true.

title: Pro feature: matching cover letter builder
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. The first thing Pro delivers: a cover letter editor that reuses the resume's name, contact details and chosen template so both documents match, with a live A4 preview and PDF download (same print/save path as the resume). Drafts live in the browser like resumes and must never overwrite a resume draft. Non-buyers can open it and see an example, and are offered Pro ($9 once) to write and download their own; buyers (`dwPay.has('pro_pass')` / `paidSkus(c)`) get it fully. Link it from the builder after a resume download ('Need a matching cover letter?'). The resume builder and its free PDF download must not change.

title: Pro feature: Word (.docx) export and several saved versions
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. Recruiters and job portals often ask for Word files. For Pro buyers add 'Download Word (.docx)' that produces a clean, editable document of exactly what is on screen (text, line breaks, bullets, non-Latin characters survive), built in the browser. Also let buyers keep several named resume versions (e.g. one per job) in the browser and switch between them without ever losing one. Non-buyers see these options with the price and a short explanation, never a broken button. Free PDF download stays exactly as it is.

title: Sell QRs That Last Pro: pricing page with a real checkout
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. Use the engine's payments capability (BRIEF.md → Payments). On /pricing keep 'Static codes free forever' as the headline promise and add Pro: `pro_lifetime`, $19 once, never expires: editable QR codes (change where a printed code points, any time) with scan counts. Button calls `dwPay.open('pro_lifetime', {next: '/editable?welcome=pro'})` (or the real path) on click; when `dwPay.ready` is false show 'Coming soon' plus the existing email list. Replace the 'Editable codes: Not available yet' card. Add 'Already bought? Unlock it here' → `dwPay.restoreUrl`. Paddle reviews the site before enabling checkout: state on /pricing and /terms that Paddle handles payment, receipts and refunds; add a plain refund policy (full refund within 14 days, reply to the receipt) on /terms or /refunds; mention Paddle on /privacy.

title: Pro feature: editable QR codes that never expire
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. What Pro buyers get: create a code whose short link (e.g. https://qrsthatlast.com/r/<id>, `/r/` is already passthrough in species.json) redirects to a destination they can change any time from a private manage link (and from any browser where they've unlocked Pro). Store codes in D1 (new migration). Show a simple scan count per code. Because the buyer paid once, the redirect must keep working forever, even if they never come back. Safety (quishing): only http/https destinations, refuse obviously deceptive destinations (IP-address hosts, punycode lookalikes of big brands, URL shorteners chains), rate-limit edits, and add a 'Report this code' link on an interstitial-free abuse page. Non-buyers see what it does and the price. Static codes stay free and unchanged.

title: Mention editable codes when people need them (honestly)
body: Owner request, TOP PRIORITY for this week: the product must be able to make its first sale. People only realise they want an editable code when they're about to print. After a download of a Link code, show one calm line under the download buttons: 'Printing this? If the link might change, an editable code lets you update it later without reprinting. $19 once, never expires.' linking to Pro. Dismissible, no pop-ups or pressure, never on Wi-Fi/contact codes. Measure with dw.track.
